1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night

The rain over Qingshi had been falling for three whole days. Lin Xiaoyu's elder sister had gone to the capital in spring, and ever since, she had been left alone to look after the little medicine shop in town.
After dark she shut the doors and windows, counted the day's takings, blew out the oil lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when hurried knocking came from below, followed by a man's voice: "Is anyone there?"
A young man stood outside, soaked through, his left arm wrapped in a strip of cloth seeping blood. He said his name was Bai Yun, and that he was one of the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need this wound dressed," Bai Yun said quietly. "I can pay. Will three thousand five hundred wen be enough?"
He drew a letter wrapped in oil paper from inside his coat. "This letter has to reach Qingfeng before the eighteenth of May."
While she bandaged him, he said with a wry smile, "If my fiancée knew I was knocking on a young woman's door in the middle of the night, she'd be jealous for sure."
Lin Xiaoyu did not take his money. She only said, "First thing tomorrow, I'll take you up the mountain."
2: At first light the two of them set out. Lin Xiaoyu carried a bamboo basket packed with dry rations, herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain they met an old woodcutter, Zhou Dashan. He set down his axe and lowered his voice: the evening before, three strangers had been asking questions at the town gate about a wounded young man.
"Xiaoyu, you two take the small path," Zhou Dashan said. "The main road isn't safe." Lin Xiaoyu thanked him.
The small path was narrow and slippery. Lin Xiaoyu walked in front, setting each foot down firmly. Bai Yun followed behind and said not a word.

At noon the rain stopped, the mountain mist slowly thinned, and the roof of Qingfeng Temple came into view in the distance. A nun stood at the temple gate—Zhao Qiuyue, the guest-prefect who received visitors for the temple.
Zhao Qiuyue took the letter, looked at the red seal on the flap, and nodded. "The abbot has waited 2 years for this letter."
Bai Yun said to Lin Xiaoyu, "I owe you my life." Lin Xiaoyu laughed. "Then next time you come, fix the roof of my medicine shop for me." Bai Yun stayed at the temple.
In the evening, Lin Xiaoyu went down the mountain alone. By the time she reached home it was already dark; she lit the lamp and sat behind the counter for a long while.
